title: Nola band at the Royal Garden, then the Pelican
summary: The Nola band started in the late 1920s, played the Royal Garden, and went to the Pelican, which was a house band job for three or four years.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What year did the Nola band start? What year was it named the Nola band, do you think? In the late 20s, sometime?
Late 20s, yeah. About 20. I was about 26, 27.
Before the Depression hit, in other words.
Yeah. What time did it? Just before. I thought, left the Louisiana Jazz on, I go to the Nola band.
And he said that you didn't use no piano. Did he else have to band you?
During that time, he wasn't using no piano, because they didn't have no piano at the place where we were playing at.
On gravel between Padilla and Jazz. And I go to the Nola band. In 1925, I think, or 26, the Pelican opened. The Pelican opened. Well, we go to the Pelican.
With the Nola band. With the baby, originally was a house band.

That was where his brother was on the place. Now, in the rhythm. He was. Oh. And we go to the Pelican. We played the Pelican about three, four years. Uh-huh. See? And I played on the Pelican. Depression was coming in. I come in all the time. I played in the Nola band until about. He said, I didn't know the band. I don't know. I don't want to play. And the Nola band was changed to the Silverton officer. That's the time old man Duce had taken the band over. Old man Duce. Not Sam Duce, but his daddy.
